answer: Agents sparrow, plume and summit must each lock a refundable bond before bidding for jobs, and each bond backs only one active identity. If an agent signs two conflicting commitments for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures to a contract that confiscates its bond. Creating names is cheap, but operating 1,000 eligible identities requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and putting it at risk whenever those identities cheat this way.
